attacks.aim: A password in a URL that also fails to parse (invalid port, port 0, %zz, %00, unknown scheme, bad arg count), --password/-p values, identity files that hold text, a .pub key or a fake PEM block, a wrong passphrase, and an INTERNAL error built from the back-end target never reach stdout or stderr; the USAGE line 'invalid URL '<x>'' must not echo the userinfo.

Percent-encoded slashes and dots (a%2F.., a%2F., a%2F, %2E%2E%2F%2E%2E) whose decoded basename is '..', '.' or empty exit 2 with no connection and write nothing in cwd or its parents; a hostile stat/list name cannot choose the local file name.

A file or symbolic link that appears at the destination while the download runs is not replaced without --overwrite (the final rename must not clobber it) and no .part file stays; with --overwrite a link swapped in is replaced itself and its target keeps its bytes.

A stream that fails after 64 KiB (typed and untyped error), a createReadStream that throws, a stream that fails before any byte, a failing disconnect after the failure, and a read-only destination directory each leave the destination as it was, no temporary file, exactly one error line with the right exit code, and one disconnect.

Raw mode is switched off when stdin errors or ends inside a UTF-8 character at the password prompt; bytes after Ctrl-C are ignored; a password split across chunks (inside a character) authenticates; a CR and its LF split across the password and host-key prompts are one line end; lines typed after 'yes' are never recorded in known_hosts; a URL host with an encoded LF, a comma, an encoded space or a wildcard is refused before any prompt or connection.

Through the real SFTP back-end: entry names with LF, CR, TAB, ESC, OSC, U+202E, U+0085, U+2028, U+2066/U+2069, DEL, a forged error line and a forged ls line each print as one escaped line with exactly 3 TABs; a hostile status text cannot forge a stderr line on ls or get; entries with an invalid time or a NaN, negative or huge size are not an INTERNAL defect (exit 1).

A hostile SFTP server answers OPENDIR or READDIR (ls), OPEN or READ (get), STAT/LSTAT/FSTAT or OPEN (put) with a bare OK that lacks the handle, entries, attributes or data. Each exits 22 with one escaped OPERATION_FAILED line that names the missing part; never INTERNAL exit 1, a hang, a second line, a leftover local file, or a remote write after a stat it could not read.

get and put of CHUNK_SIZE-1, CHUNK_SIZE, CHUNK_SIZE+1, 2*CHUNK_SIZE, 32 KiB-1/32 KiB/32 KiB+1, WINDOW*CHUNK_SIZE and +1 bytes are byte-identical; a server that returns half, one byte less, or 1 KiB more than each READ asks gives a byte-identical file or one exit-22 line and no file; the CHUNK_SIZE doc comment's limits hold for the constant and the WINDOW comment's bytes in flight equal WINDOW*CHUNK_SIZE.
